states: An isolated Pro development runtime showed an OIDC user by the mutable display name Alice Example, with alice@example.com and OIDC · okta as secondary identity context while retaining the stable sso:oidc:okta:browser-subject authorization principal.
The Manage Access dialog used the readable identity in its title and exposed email and provider context while preserving the current Viewer role and effective-permissions preview.

The removal confirmation clearly stated that roles and active Pulse sessions are removed, that the upstream identity-provider account is not disabled, and that a later authorized SSO login can recreate the Pulse identity.

A successful removal returned the filtered list to no matching SSO user and displayed User access removed for Alice Example; an attempted self-removal retained the admin row and displayed You cannot remove your own user access.

At 390x844 the page remained exactly 390 pixels wide, the shared table shell provided horizontal access to both actions, and the 358-pixel confirmation dialog stayed inside the viewport without clipping or horizontal document overflow.
